---
title: "10. Capstone: plan your own AI project"
subtitle: "Day 2 · 14:45–16:00 · Group work and pitches"
---

The capstone turns the workshop into a plan you can take home. In small groups, participants choose a real problem — ideally one from the Day 1 icebreaker board — and design an AI project on one page.

## How it runs

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| 5 min | Form groups of 3–4 around a shared interest; pick one problem |
| 40 min | Fill in the [AI project canvas](../resources/project-canvas.qmd) |
| 25 min | 3-minute pitch per group, 2 minutes of questions |
| 5 min | Vote: most promising project, best evaluation plan |

## What a strong plan has

- **A sharp question.** "Predict *Fusarium* head blight risk per field, two weeks before flowering" beats "use AI for disease".
- **Data that exist or can be collected**, with an honest count of samples, sites and seasons.
- **A baseline** — what is done today, or the simplest possible model.
- **An honest evaluation** that matches the real use: which groups must be kept apart (sites, years, families, batches)?
- **Named risks:** confounding, missing populations, data ownership, what happens when the model is wrong.
- **A first step for next month** — a pilot that is small enough to actually do.

## Feedback questions for pitches

1. What would convince you the model works on a new farm, season or population?
2. What is the simplest model you would try first?
3. What could the model learn that isn't biology (batch, site, photographer, date)?
4. Who would use the result, and what would they do differently?

## After the workshop

Groups that want to take their plan further can bring it to the follow-up clinic (see the [Instructor notes](../instructors.qmd)). Keep the canvas: it is the outline of a project proposal.
